questions.scenario: Your best friend is having a panic attack right before the dreaded Math Board Exam. How do you calm them down?

options.A: I make them do 5 minutes of 'Anulom Vilom' (alternate nostril breathing) and stretch their shoulders to physically release the tension.
options.B: I quote a practical lesson from the Bhagavad Gita about focusing purely on the 'Karma' (action) and detaching from the result.
options.C: I put my earphones in their ears and play a super calming, lo-fi instrumental flute track to completely change their vibe.
options.D: I take charge, organize their geometry box, check their admit card, and confidently walk them to the exam hall door.

questions.scenario: Your parents drag you to a 3-hour long spiritual Satsang/Kirtan on a Sunday morning. What are you doing there?

options.A: Sitting with perfectly straight posture cross-legged on the carpet, focusing on the rhythm of my breath.
options.B: Listening closely to the Guru's discourse, logically analyzing the philosophical meaning behind the ancient stories.
options.C: Totally lost in the rhythm of the tabla and the harmonium, loving the musical and emotional energy of the bhajans.
options.D: Looking around to observe how well the crowd is managed, the seating arrangement, and the food distribution (langar) system.

questions.scenario: Your close friend just went through a terrible breakup and is crying uncontrollably. How do you support them?

options.A: Take them for a long morning walk or a quick run in the local park to get their endorphins pumping and body moving.
options.B: Have a deep, late-night conversation explaining the psychology of attachment and why letting go is necessary for personal growth.
options.C: Create a cozy vibe in their room, light a mild incense stick (agarbatti), and make them listen to soothing music to cry it out safely.
options.D: Plan a complete weekend distraction itinerary—booking a movie, deciding the food, and managing the whole friend group's schedule.

questions.scenario: It's June 21st (International Yoga Day), and your school is hosting a massive morning event on the main ground.

options.A: I am right at the front on the stage, perfectly demonstrating the Surya Namaskar because my physical form is flawless.
options.B: I am reading the anchor's script, explaining the ancient history of Patanjali's Yoga Sutras and the deeper meaning behind the poses.
options.C: I am in charge of selecting the perfect, peaceful background instrumental music to play over the school's loudspeakers.
options.D: I am coordinating with the PT teacher to ensure the 500 yoga mats are perfectly aligned and students are seated in straight rows.

questions.scenario: Your family goes on a vacation to Rishikesh. What is the highlight of the trip for you?

options.A: Waking up at 5 AM to do a rigorous, energizing yoga session right next to the freezing cold waters of the river Ganga.
options.B: Visiting the ancient ashrams, buying a book on Vedanta, and talking to the local monks about the true meaning of life.
options.C: Sitting by the ghats during the evening Aarti, completely mesmerized by the chanting, the bells, and the visual beauty of the floating diyas.
options.D: Calculating how the local ashrams manage thousands of tourists daily, and figuring out the business model of wellness camps.

questions.scenario: You've had a terrible, exhausting day at school and evening tuition. What is your go-to way to find peace at home?

options.A: Doing some deep neck stretches and a quick 10-minute physical workout on my bedroom floor to sweat out the stress.
options.B: Reading a thought-provoking book or watching a podcast about human psychology, karma, and the subconscious mind.
options.C: Turning off the harsh tubelight, switching on a warm lamp, and listening to a rain-sounds or singing bowl track on YouTube.
options.D: Decluttering my messy study table, making a neat to-do list for tomorrow, and organizing my thoughts into a clear plan.

questions.scenario: If someone scrolled through your Instagram Reels or YouTube recommendations, what would they mostly find?

options.A: Fitness challenges, mobility drills, and step-by-step tutorials on how to do a perfect headstand or backbend.
options.B: Long podcast clips of modern monks or intellectuals discussing life advice, philosophy, and mindset shifts.
options.C: Satisfying aesthetic videos, calming visual ASMR, and trending lo-fi Indian classical music remixes.
options.D: Vlogs about 'Day in the life of a CEO', travel itineraries for spiritual retreats, and productivity hacks.

questions.scenario: A junior asks you for advice on how to survive the extreme pressure of 10th standard. What is your core message?

options.A: You need to fix your sleep cycle and exercise daily. A physically healthy body handles mental stress much better.
options.B: Understand the 'why' behind your stress. Detach your self-worth from your mark sheet—it's just an illusion created by society.
options.C: Find a creative outlet. Whenever you panic, close your eyes, put on some calming music, and just breathe into the sound.
options.D: Time management is everything. Let me help you build a solid study timetable so you don't panic at the last minute.

questions.scenario: You are given an empty room on the school terrace to turn into a 'Wellness Zone' for students. How do you set it up?

options.A: I'm bringing in thick yoga mats, foam rollers, and leaving lots of open space for physical stretching and movement.
options.B: I'm bringing in a mini-library filled with books on philosophy, self-help, and comfortable chairs for deep, logical discussions.
options.C: I'm bringing in wind chimes, fairy lights, aromatic diffusers, and a Bluetooth speaker to create a deeply ambient vibe.
options.D: I'm creating a clear timetable, setting up a booking system, and proposing a budget to the Principal for regular maintenance.

questions.scenario: When you think about your ultimate future goal, what brings you the most peace?

options.A: Having a perfectly healthy, flexible, and energetic body well into old age, and inspiring others to move and heal.
options.B: Unlocking the deepest mysteries of the human mind and writing a book that fundamentally changes how people view life.
options.C: Creating beautiful, safe, artistic spaces where people can instantly feel healed just by walking in and listening.
options.D: Building and managing a massive, successful wellness empire that employs hundreds of people and helps thousands.

Yoga_Instructor.title: Yoga & Breathwork Instructor
Yoga_Instructor.primary_match_text: The Physical Healer! You believe the mind and body are deeply connected. You love movement, fitness, and taking physical action to find peace and help others heal.
Yoga_Instructor.day_in_the_life: Conducting morning sunrise yoga batches, correcting postures, teaching deep Pranayama to stressed corporate workers, and living a highly active, disciplined lifestyle.
Yoga_Instructor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream, Science/Arts preferred) -> B.Sc or B.A in Yoga / Physical Education -> Complete an AYUSH Ministry recognized Yoga Teacher Training Course (TTC 200/500 hours).

Vedic_Scholar.title: Philosophical / Vedic Scholar
Vedic_Scholar.primary_match_text: The Deep Thinker! You are highly analytical and love diving into the 'why' behind human existence, using logic, psychology, and ancient wisdom to solve modern problems.
Vedic_Scholar.day_in_the_life: Reading heavy texts like the Upanishads or modern psychology books, giving lectures or hosting podcasts on life advice, and counseling people through their mental blocks.
Vedic_Scholar.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Humanities/Arts preferred) -> B.A in Philosophy, Psychology, or Sanskrit -> Master's (M.A) and Ph.D. in Eastern Philosophy or Clinical Psychology.

Sound_Healer.title: Sound Healer / Guided Meditation Artist
Sound_Healer.primary_match_text: The Vibe Creator! You are highly creative, artistic, and sensitive. You use aesthetics, music, and beautiful environments to help people relax and escape their anxiety.
Sound_Healer.day_in_the_life: Playing Tibetan singing bowls, curating incredibly relaxing playlists, recording guided meditation audio for apps, and designing stunning zen spaces for therapy sessions.
Sound_Healer.alternative_match_text: Music Therapist, Wellness Interior Designer, Art Therapist
Sound_Healer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream, Arts preferred) -> B.A in Psychology, Fine Arts, or Music -> Specialized Certification in Sound Healing, Music Therapy, or Alternative Medicine.

Retreat_Organizer.title: Spiritual Retreat Organizer
Retreat_Organizer.primary_match_text: The Wellness Mastermind! You have a sharp business brain but care deeply about people's peace. You love organizing, managing, and leading massive wellness projects.
Retreat_Organizer.day_in_the_life: Managing a massive wellness ashram in the mountains, negotiating with travel agencies, handling finances, and ensuring guests have a flawlessly peaceful, zero-stress experience.
Retreat_Organizer.alternative_match_text: Event Manager, Hospitality Director, Travel Entrepreneur
Retreat_Organizer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Commerce or Arts preferred) -> BBA, B.Com, or Bachelor of Hotel Management (BHM) -> MBA in Hospitality, Tourism Management, or Event Management.
